title: Grading passes unit commands to sh -c in double quotes, so the outer shell expands $ before the unit runs
body:
Grading wraps unit commands as `timeout N sh -c ${JSON.stringify(cmd)}` (evals/units/screening.ts:390 and the test call). The double-quoted nesting lets the outer shell expand `$x`, `$?` and `$(...)` before the inner shell runs: the python install `for x in test tests dev; do ... -e ".[$x]"` installs `.[]` (no test extras). 2 committed units carry `$` in install/test. Found while writing the t-k7gv1wt HOME test (its probe's `$?` read the outer shell's status).
Acceptance: a unit command containing `$x` and `$?` sees them in the inner shell (regression test in test/evals/screening-units.test.ts at gradeWorktree level); quoting by single-quote escaping, never JSON.stringify. Re-verify the 2 affected units; this must land before t-zk8cmrz re-verifies all 73.
Proof: node --test test/evals/screening-units.test.ts exits 0 with a nested-dollar regression test
